clue.text: Foolish fellow is stern after new cut in earnings

indicators.note: after says the stern comes behind the other pieces
cut means the word for earnings loses its final letter

parts.note: earnings are one's income
the poop is the raised deck at a ship's stern

explanation.surface: A complaint about a pay cut, with someone being stern about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last E of INCOME to leave INCOM; N goes in front and POOP follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a nitwit or idiot is a silly, foolish man.

clue.text: Map feature no obstacle — one's in the lead

indicators.note: in the lead says this piece goes at the front of the answer

parts.note: one is I, and one's is read as one is, giving I plus S
O looks like zero, nothing, so no gives O
a bar is a barrier or obstacle

explanation.surface: A route with no obstacle, and someone leading the race.
explanation.definitionFit: A line on a weather map joining places of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Is he always having to change trains?

definitions.text: Is he always having to change trains?

parts.words: Is he always having to change trains?
parts.note: a person who travels daily to work by rail; the change is not a swap of trains but a daily to-and-fro journey

explanation.definitionFit: A daily rail traveller to and from work is forever on and off trains, the cryptic sense of changing.

clue.text: He backs a one-man show as a rule

definitions.text: He backs a one-man show as a rule

parts.words: He backs a one-man show as a rule
parts.note: a one-man show is read as rule by a single sovereign, and he backs (supports) that form of government

explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of rule by a king or queen backs government by one person.

clue.text: I comply awkwardly, being of Pisa?

indicators.note: awkwardly says the letters of the words I comply are clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone grudgingly obeying, wondering whether they belong to Pisa.
explanation.walkthrough: Ancient Pisa (in Elis, not the Italian city) presided over the games at Olympia, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Pisa lay beside Olympia and ran its games, so something of Pisa could be described as relating to Olympia.

clue.text: Met quietly to give assistance'

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
aid is help or assistance

explanation.surface: Someone met discreetly in order to offer help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met' looks like a meeting; it is the settling of a bill, as in met the costs.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a bill is to settle it, the past tense being settled.

clue.text: Band support reason for cancelling service

parts.note: a brace is a support or prop
in tennis a let voids a serve that clips the net, so it must be taken again

explanation.surface: A band's backer calls off a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests church; it is a tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: A bangle or wristlet is a decorative band worn round the wrist.

clue.text: Even cigars may give grounds for complaint

indicators.note: may give suggests the letters of Even cigars can be rearranged to produce something new

explanation.surface: Even cigars can cause people to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: grievances are complaints or reasons to feel wronged.

clue.text: He worships one like Miss Spenlow, some say

indicators.note: some say means the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: Dora Spenlow is David Copperfield's child-bride in Dickens, so one like her is a Dora

explanation.surface: A devotee who worships someone like Dickens's Dora Spenlow.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent 'a Dora' is said the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A worshipper is one who loves someone devotedly.

clue.text: Seasonal gift for a swineherd? Yes indeed

parts.note: a swineherd is literally a hog man
ay is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: Asking whether a pig-keeper gets a Christmas present, and answering yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scottish word for New Year's Eve also means a gift given then; this is Scottish usage.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland the word also names a New Year present, a gift given at the turn of the year.

clue.text: Dwarf holds one in lake — it's hardly fair

indicators.note: in puts the dwarf with his one inside the word for lake

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pond

indicators.note: holds means the dwarf's name contains the letter for one

parts.note: Doc is one of Snow White's seven dwarfs
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dwarf grasping something in a lake, judged not quite fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts I inside DOC to make DIOC, and 'in' puts that inside MERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only middling or second-rate is barely of fair quality.

clue.text: Sandstone used to remove sulphur from corn

indicators.note: remove says the letter for sulphur is taken away from the grain word

parts.note: grist is corn for grinding
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Sandstone is used to clean sulphur off grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Gritstone, often called by its short form, is a coarse sandstone.

clue.text: Where great resistance may be offered to students of race

definitions.text: Where great resistance may be offered to students of race

parts.note: grand means great or splendid
a stand is resistance, as in making a stand

explanation.surface: Fierce opposition being met by students of ethnicity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'students of race' suggests ethnic studies; they are racegoers studying the horses.
explanation.definitionFit: The main covered seating at a racecourse is where race spectators sit and watch.

clue.text: Fur is unpleasantly cold in part of Asia

indicators.note: in means the word for cold sits inside the Asian country

parts.note: China is a country in Asia
a chill is an unpleasant coldness

explanation.surface: Fur feels uncomfortably cold somewhere in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft grey pelt of a small South American rodent is a prized fur.

clue.text: Plan soldiers employ to find drink

parts.note: a chart is a plan or map
RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
to use is to employ

explanation.surface: A plan for using soldiers to find something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A liqueur made by Carthusian monks is a drink.

clue.text: Under pressure, it's a measure done with air somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of done and air are put together in some new way

explanation.surface: A measure carried out with air when under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A barometer that works without liquid is an instrument measuring atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Former page permitted to be outspoken

parts.note: ex means former
licit means lawful or permitted

explanation.surface: An ex-page is allowed to speak frankly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: frank, plain speech states things clearly and openly.

clue.text: Fine caper cut by a zealot

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: cut by means the word for caper is split open by the letter A

parts.note: an antic is a caper or prank

explanation.surface: A fine prank interrupted by a fanatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an extremist or fervent enthusiast.

clue.text: Almost appointed eccentric as a rival church leader

indicators.note: eccentric says the remaining letters are arranged oddly
almost means the word appointed loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone nearly appointed, an oddball, setting up as a rival to the church's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A pope set up in opposition to the canonically elected pontiff.

clue.text: Goddess encountered among wild creatures

indicators.note: among puts the word for encountered inside the word for the wild animals

parts.note: deer are wild animals
met means encountered

explanation.surface: A goddess was met among wild animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of the harvest and agriculture.

clue.text: Carriage intended, it's said, to follow exile

indicators.note: to follow puts the sound piece after the exile word

parts.note: to deport is to exile

indicators.note: it's said means the word for intended is taken as heard

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A carriage was intended to carry someone into exile.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage here means bearing or posture, how one holds oneself.

clue.text: Spinners are people of the best type

definitions.meaning: spinning toys that whirl on a point
the very best people, as in being the absolute best

explanation.definitionFit: Spinning toys whirl on a point, and colloquially the best people are the very top ones.

clue.text: Birds see appeal in seeds

indicators.note: in puts the word for appeal inside the word for seeds

parts.note: pips are fruit seeds
it is sex appeal

explanation.surface: Birds notice something attractive among seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Small brown songbirds of the wagtail family, such as the meadow kind.

clue.text: Celtic railway briefly displaced this conveyance

indicators.note: displaced says the letters are moved out of their order

parts.note: RY is a short form for railway

explanation.surface: A Celtic railway line pushed out by this vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-wheeled cycle is a means of conveyance.

clue.text: Ready to appear in Corsica shortly

indicators.note: in says the letters are found within the words Corsica shortly

explanation.surface: Someone ready to show up in Corsica soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready, short for ready money, means money in hand.

clue.text: Lawrence takes universal pick-me-up. It's German

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia
U is the film certificate for universal
a tonic is a pick-me-up

explanation.surface: Lawrence has a universal restorative, and it is German.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the Germanic peoples, so used for German.

clue.text: Conventional remarks of a poet, do we hear?

indicators.note: do we hear asks whether the poet's possessive matches by sound

parts.note: Alfred Noyes was an English poet; of him is Noyes's

explanation.surface: Asking whether we can hear a poet's conventional remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Making the right sounds means saying the expected, polite things.

clue.text: Plain sagacity of Incitatus, presumably

definitions.meaning: Incitatus was Caligula's horse, so his wits would be those of a horse

explanation.definitionFit: Plain common sense, and literally the intelligence of a horse like Caligula's Incitatus.
